Mackenzie Ryan Mackenzie is in his first term as a Member of the United States House of Representatives. He represents the 7th Congressional District of Pennsylvania, which covers all of Lehigh, Northampton, and Carbon Counties and part of Monroe County. Ryan serves on three committees in the U.S. House: Education and the Workforce, Foreign Affairs, and Homeland Security. Through these committee assignments, he continues his work to improve education and workforce development, bring about peace through American strength, and advocate for safe and secure communities. Before being elected to Congress, Ryan served as a Member of the Pennsylvania House of Representatives from 2012-2024. During his time in the state House, he was Republican chair of the Labor & Industry Committee and co-chair of the International Relations Caucus. Without action, the average taxpayer would have seen a  22% tax hike . After four years of rising prices, working families, seniors, and small businesses in the Greater Lehigh Valley, that outcome was unacceptable. Mackenzie Applauds House Passage of Stop Insider Trading Act | Congressman Ryan Mackenzie Skip to main content Phone:  (202) 225-6411 Email Me Address:  121 Cannon Office Building, Washington, DC 20515   Mackenzie Applauds House Passage of Stop Insider Trading Act Image July 23, 2026 Press Release Washington, D.C. — Congressman Ryan Mackenzie (PA-07), representing the Lehigh Valley and the Poconos, applauded the passage in the U.S. House this week of bipartisan legislation to crack down on stock trading by members of Congress.  The  Stop Insider Trading Act , of which the Congressman was an original cosponsor, prohibits members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent children from purchasing individual stocks while serving in office. Additionally, the legislation requires advance public disclosure before any sales of covered securities and establishes significant financial penalties for violations. “Members of Congress are sent to Washington to serve their constituents, not themselves,”  said Congressman Mackenzie. “The American people deserve confidence that their elected officials are making decisions based on what’s best for their country — not their own financial interests. The epidemic of lawmakers leveraging insider information for personal profits has degraded trust and accountability, which is why I’ve co-sponsored several pieces of legislation aimed at cracking down on this practice. Much more work remains in the fight to reform Washington, but passage of the  Stop Insider Trading Act  marks an important step toward providing a government which prioritizes the needs of the American people.”  Since taking office, Congressman Mackenzie has consistently supported efforts to strengthen ethics and increase transparency in Congress. In addition to co-sponsoring the  Stop Insider Trading Act , he has also co-sponsored two similar pieces of bipartisan legislation. The  Transparent Representation Upholding Service and Trust  (TRUST) in Congress Act requires members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent children to place certain financial assets into qualified blind trusts. Mackenzie Introduces Bipartisan Resolution Recognizing Medicare's 61st Anniversary | Congressman Ryan Mackenzie Skip to main content Phone:  (202) 225-6411 Email Me Address:  121 Cannon Office Building, Washington, DC 20515   Mackenzie Introduces Bipartisan Resolution Recognizing Medicare's 61st Anniversary Image July 30, 2026 Press Release Washington, D.C.  – This week, Congressman Ryan Mackenzie (PA-07), representing the Lehigh Valley and the Poconos, introduced a bipartisan resolution recognizing the 61st anniversary of Medicare's enactment and honoring the program's enduring role in providing health coverage to older Americans and individuals with disabilities. The resolution is led by Congressman Ryan Mackenzie and Congressman Eugene Vindman (VA-07). It is joined by Representatives Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), Monica De La Cruz (TX-15), Dina Titus (NV-01), Don Davis (NC-01), Claudia Tenney (NY-24), and Michael Lawler (NY-17). Signed into law by President Lyndon B. Johnson on July 30, 1965, Medicare has provided health insurance coverage to millions of Americans for more than six decades. Today, the program serves nearly 70 million seniors and individuals with disabilities. "For 61 years, Medicare has provided millions of Americans with access to quality health care and greater financial security," said Congressman Mackenzie . "This bipartisan resolution recognizes Medicare's lasting impact while honoring the healthcare providers, caregivers, and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services personnel who work every day to ensure beneficiaries receive the care they depend on. Congress must continue to support, protect, and strengthen Medicare for current beneficiaries
